answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with staked, one-per-identity credentials audited by a public randomness beacon. Each agent locks a bond and gets a single nullifier that marks its messages like indelible pigment, so two accounts sharing it are slashed. Every round the beacon samples auditors who verify each bond and nullifier; a hoard of fakes collapses at its nadir once one is checked. The attacker must fund a fresh bond per fake identity, and any audited duplicate forfeits the pool, so the cost rises linearly with the attack's size.
